input.summary:
P7 gallery furnished in parts/room-46.mjs: a red bed (x86) and an orange bed (x93), each with its head on the house wall at z8, plus a barrel nightstand with a flower pot and a spruce-stair chair on the front edge. Each unit has a hanging lantern at y10; the doorway cells x88 and x91 at z8 stay clear.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with the part at 6 placed blocks and no refused or off-palette writes. In that build the bed and chair calls placed nothing (no shell walls yet), so the real furnishing is not in it yet.
Verified only on a scratch copy with a deck at y7 and walls: room reads OK, 20/20 floor cells reachable, minimum light 10, no dark cells, fit OK.
left: The real build has no shell here (the gallery deck y7, the walls and the pier are other parts' work), so bed_set refused both beds and the chairs and lanterns placed nothing or floated. Rerun make.sh and `$MCD room` once the shell lands, to confirm the head walls at z9 y8 and the lantern ceilings.

Rockers were not built: rocker()'s back trapdoor would sit on the lane cells x87/x92 z8 in front of the doors. Spruce-stair chairs stand in for them on z7; a proper rocker needs the rail or wall behind it, which the shell decides.
No `$MCD rooms` render was made: the other parts are still stubs in this copy, so a render would show an empty gallery.
plan.md Notes carries the furnishing line; the elements.md gallery items are the shell's (P4 fittings) and were not ticked by this part.

waste.what: Checking the furnishing needed a scratch script to rebuild a deck, walls and a ceiling by hand, since the room tool can't judge the room without the shell.
waste.cost: about 3 retries and one scratch Grid script of roughly 30 set() calls
waste.tool: A `mcd room --assume-shell` mode (or a `--stub-shell` option) that lays a floor, walls and ceiling from rooms.json's box and openings, so a room can be judged before its shell exists.

waste.what: Working out the lane, bed head and chair cells on the 10x2 gallery by hand, cell by cell, to keep the doorway's first cell clear.
